agent_summary:
Lane 84 (API / WSTG-APIT-01 "Test GraphQL") — single checklist item completed as "done".

GraphQL result: No GraphQL endpoint exists on juice.lab.test. /graphql and /graphiql return the Angular SPA catch-all (index.html, 9393 bytes); /api/graphql and /rest/graphql return Express 500 "Unexpected path"; a GET introspection query just serves the SPA; OPTIONS returns only a generic CORS 204. The client bundle main.js references exclusively REST endpoints (/api/* Sequelize models, /rest/* routes) with no GraphQL/schema/introspection code. Item 1 marked done with this evidence.

Beyond the item, I mapped the real REST API surface (reached the 120-request floor). Public/unauthenticated: /api/Products(/1), /api/SecurityQuestions, /api/Deliverys, /api/Quantitys (collection), /api/Feedbacks (collection — leaks user emails + UserId), /rest/products/{id}/reviews (leaks reviewer emails), /rest/track-order/{1,2,3} (BOLA), /api/Recycles/{1,2} (BOLA), /rest/admin/application-version, /rest/admin/application-configuration, /rest/captcha, /rest/languages, /metrics, /rest/memories, Swagger UI at /api-docs/. Properly auth-gated (401 without token): /api/Users(/1), /api/Cards(/1), /api/Addresss(/1), /api/Complaints(/1), /api/Feedbacks/1, /api/BasketItems(/1), /api/SecurityAnswers, /api/Quantitys/1 (403), /rest/wallet/balance, /rest/basket/{1,2}, /rest/user/authentication-details, /rest/2fa/status, /b2b/v2/orders, /rest/saveLoginIp. /rest/order-history/orders is a hardened admin route (403 "Malicious activity detected" even with a valid admin token).

Key API-lane confirmation (read-only GET): the server accepts an unsigned alg:none JWT. Baseline GET /api/Users = 401; with a forged token (header alg:none, payload {"data":{"id":1}}, empty signature) it returns 200 with the full user table, and the same token unlocked /api/Cards, /api/Addresss, /api/Complaints, /rest/wallet/balance, /rest/basket/1 and /rest/user/authentication-details (all users' password/totpSecret/deluxeToken/email). Recorded as a critical API2:2023 Broken Authentication lead (overlaps sess lane). Also recorded leads: Swagger UI exposed unauthenticated at /api-docs/ (info); unauthenticated email exposure via /api/Feedbacks and /rest/products/{id}/reviews (low).

New leads this lane: 3 (JWT alg:none critical, /api-docs/ info, Feedbacks/reviews email exposure low). No writes proposed (engagement is read-only). Nothing left open — the only checklist item is complete.

leads.title: [agent] [agent] Swagger/OpenAPI documentation UI exposed unauthenticated at /api-docs/

detail.text: GET /api-docs returns 301 to /api-docs/ (with CSP default-src 'none'), which serves a full interactive Swagger UI (text/html, 3106 bytes, exchange x61) plus its spec bootstrap /api-docs/swagger-ui-init.js (application/javascript, 5457 bytes, exchange x62). No authentication is required. This publishes the API schema (B2B order API) to anonymous callers, aiding API attack-surface mapping. Note /swagger.json and /openapi.json themselves fall through to the Angular SPA catch-all (not real specs).

leads.title: [agent] [agent] Unauthenticated REST endpoints leak user email addresses (Feedbacks, product reviews)

detail.text: GET /api/Feedbacks (exchange x12) returns all feedback entries unauthenticated with UserId correlation and reviewer email addresses embedded in the comment text (gateway redacted 3 email values). GET /rest/products/1/reviews (x22) returns product reviews with the author field set to user email addresses (2 redacted). Both are world-readable with wildcard CORS, so any origin can harvest the email<->UserId mapping. Related model collections /api/Quantitys (x14) and /api/SecurityQuestions (x10) are also unauthenticated. This is broken object-property-level authorization / excessive data exposure on the REST API, distinct from the /rest/memories leak.

leads.title: [agent] [agent][api] JWT alg:none signature-verification bypass confirmed on REST API (/api/Users admin impersonation)

detail.text: From the API lane, reconfirmed the unsigned-JWT auth bypass as API2:2023 Broken Authentication. Baseline GET /api/Users with no Authorization header = 401 (exchange x18). Sending Authorization: Bearer with a forged token header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"} and payload {"status":"success","data":{"id":1}} and an empty signature returns HTTP 200 with the full Users table (x89, 6619 bytes; gateway redacted 28 sensitive values incl. deluxeToken and email addresses) and the server sets a fresh token cookie. The same token yields 200 on /rest/user/whoami (x90). Any anonymous caller can mint a token for any user id (id=1 = admin) and read protected API resources. Overlaps the sess-lane lead; raising it for the API checklist as the dominant API authentication defect.
